title: Move a familiar rule to Python
outcome: Translate the pricing rule without changing its behaviour.
story: Amina needs the same correct price on her website and at the service that accepts orders. Use a familiar problem to learn Python before learning a server framework.

frames.explanation: Five items cost 500 cents before a ten percent discount. The rule is the same in either language.
A language change must preserve input validation as well as the happy path.

sections.title: Start with what you already know
paragraphs: Python has variables, conditions, lists, dictionaries, and functions. These are the same ideas you used in JavaScript. def introduces a function; return sends its result back. A dictionary such as {"total": 200} resembles a JavaScript object.

Python uses indentation to group statements. Put four spaces before the lines inside a function or if block. You do not put braces around those blocks. Read the program from the top and follow the values, rather than memorising punctuation.

sections.title: Use integer money
paragraphs: Keep amounts in cents. items = price * quantity computes the subtotal. // performs floor division: 505 // 10 is 50, so the discount stays a whole number. Write down the rounding policy before implementing it.
The conditional expression discount = items // 10 if quantity >= 5 else 0 chooses one of two values. You can also write a normal if block. Both forms must produce the same agreed prices.

sections.title: Keep a clear function boundary
paragraphs: This function accepts two numbers and returns a dictionary. It does not read a web page or connect to a database. That small boundary makes the pricing rule easy to test and reuse in a server.

Validate both inputs before multiplying. In Python, bool is related to int, so type(value) is int deliberately rejects True and False here. Raise ValueError when the caller breaks the contract. An API will later turn that into a useful response.

sections.title: Run it outside the browser
paragraphs: The exercise runs actual Python in a browser runtime. The downloadable kit also runs with Python on your computer. Use python --version, then python check.py in the extracted folder. Some systems use python3 instead.

A backend is a program that responds to requests and owns shared rules and data. Merely rewriting a function in Python does not create a server. In lesson 15 you will call this sort of function from a real HTTP endpoint.

words.meaning: Spaces that identify a group of Python statements.
The service responsible for shared rules and data.

explanation: def creates a reusable rule with two inputs.
The subtotal and discount use whole cents.
return gives the caller a structured result.

exercise.title: A Python price quote
exercise.brief: Write quote(price, quantity). Return items and total in cents, subtract ten percent for five or more items, and reject inputs outside the contract.

steps.title: Calculate the subtotal
steps.task: Return items and total, both equal to price times quantity.
steps.hint: Use a dictionary with the two required keys.
steps.solution:
def quote(price, quantity):
    return {"items": price * quantity, "total": price * quantity}

steps.title: Apply the bulk discount
steps.task: For quantity at least five, subtract items // 10 from total.
steps.hint: Calculate items once, then calculate discount separately.

steps.title: Guard the boundary
steps.task: Reject non-integer or negative inputs with ValueError. Booleans are not valid quantities.
steps.hint: Use type(value) is int for both inputs before arithmetic.

cases.label: Negative quantity
cases.why: Bad input must not become a price.

cases.label: A boolean quantity
cases.why: Python booleans must not silently become quantities.

project.title: The same quote in two languages
project.brief: Run the JavaScript and Python pricing rules against an agreed set of order examples. Explain any intentional difference before changing code.
deliverables: A shared table of expected quotes.

milestones.title: Prepare the contract
actions: Write down inputs, outputs, rounding, and rejection rules.
Choose ordinary, threshold, and invalid examples.

milestones.title: Translate and run
actions: Implement the same rule in JavaScript.
Compare each result with the agreed table.

milestones.title: Explain and extend
actions: Add shipping as a separate input.
Document how each language reports an invalid input.
Have another person run both commands.

acceptance: Both languages match the agreed valid quotes.
Both commands work from the README.

tests.expected: The documented order of calculations is followed.

project.extension: Add a maximum order size and test its exact boundary in both languages.
reflection: Where did indentation change how you read the program?
Why should the API call this rule rather than copy it?
